open_questions: Centroid is inconclusive (no sector with a clear difference image) - on-target difference imaging would formally rule out a background blend; photometric confirmation in another aperture would help

Star shows 4816 ppm variability at 5.716 d with period near 1/3 of orbital period (ratio 2.4779) and RUWE 1.187/excess_noise_sig 2.838 - RV on this active M dwarf will be needed to confirm planets vs hierarchical binary and to measure mass
Density fit shows star_density_penalty 25.18 and grazing impact parameter 0.9615 - grazing geometry degeneracies remain, but radius, duration and shape together still best fit a 3.1 Rearth planet
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 14.2-day, flat-bottomed dip repeating identically three times that matches the size and duration expected of a ~3 Earth-radius world around this small M dwarf. There is no sign of odd/even variation, a secondary eclipse, or a nearby star that could mimic the signal, which disfavours a background eclipsing binary. The star is spotted variable, but the signal period is not tied to the stellar rotation, supporting a planet as the best current explanation pending extra confirmation.

reasons.why: No odd/even depth difference, disfavors eclipsing binary at twice period (28.4 d).
Light curve is not V-shaped; favours a flat/domed transit over grazing stellar eclipse.
Implied radius is planet-sized (3.07 Earth radii) for TIC radius 0.4471, well below stellar regime.
Duration matches central transit expectation (observed 2.999 h vs central 2.575 h) on a main-sequence star.
Three individual transits are mutually consistent and together make SNR 15.9/15.85 refit; no domination by a few bad events.
No star within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can plausibly produce the dip with a ≤25% eclipse, so blended neighbour is unlikely; inconclusive centroid does not indicate off-target.
